fighterA.name: White Lantern Kyle Rayner

dossier.style: Creative combat with white light constructs. Utilizes the power of the Seven Spectra to create infinite offensive and defensive solutions.
dossier.advantage: Absolute versatility and regeneration. White light allows him to heal wounds, recreate matter, and adapt to any threat.
dossier.mentality: Persistent and resourceful. Does not panic under pressure, but constantly seeks a creative gap in the opponent's defense, escalating power as needed.
dossier.quote: In brightest day, there will be light, To cleanse the soul and set wrongs right. When darkness falls, look to the skies, A new dawn comes, let there be light!

victories: Guardians of the Universe (temporary transformation / dominance)

powers: White Lantern spectrum access, construct creation, healing, life-force manipulation, and teleportation.
tools: Life Equation access and wide ring-based utility for offense, defense, and restoration.
weaknesses: Ring dependence and concentration dependence for top-end effects.
The strongest outcomes still require setup time and execution window.

crucialFeats: Survives the Source Wall and returns with the Life Equation.
Unwillingly creates life by his presence.
Changes The Source, code on which the reality runs.

fighterB.name: Dr. Manhattan

dossier.style: Total control over matter and atoms. Does not fight in a traditional way – simply disintegrates enemies or removes them from reality with a single gesture.
dossier.advantage: Omnipresence and awareness of time. Sees the future of the fight before it begins, which combined with molecular manipulation makes him elusive.
dossier.mentality: Detached observer with mathematical coldness. Acts without emotion, treating the clash as an inevitable process with a predetermined outcome.
dossier.quote: Yes. I see now. Everything ends.

victories: Silk Spectre / Laurie (localized reality coercion, non-lethal)

powers: Atomic manipulation, matter disintegration/reconstruction, self-reassembly, and timeline-level perception.
tools: Space-time intervention and causal interference instead of a regular fight.
weaknesses: In some portrayals, passivity or detachment delays decisive action.
Traditional close-quarters combat expression is narrower than his raw reality-control profile.

crucialFeats: Experiences all time lines at once.

tactical-board.headline: TACTICAL BOARD // KYLE VS MANHATTAN
tactical-board.subtitle: Willpower versus Causality
tactical-board.lane: Kyle needs a real action window. Manhattan wins by collapsing the setup before it becomes a fight.

final-summary.headline: FINAL SUMMARY
final-summary.subtitle: Summary
final-summary.winner: Dr. Manhattan leads, but the fight is conditional
final-summary.line1: Kyle wins the paper comparison, 88.11 to 83.33.
final-summary.line2: Manhattan leads the default fight because he owns the better first move and attacks the setup itself.
final-summary.line3: Kyle flips the matchup only if Life Equation access is full and Manhattan does not proactively collapse the setup.

battle-dynamics.headline: BATTLE DYNAMICS
battle-dynamics.subtitle: How the fight changes minute by minute.
battle-dynamics.phase1: Manhattan is strongest before symmetry forms and while the setup still looks fragile.
battle-dynamics.phase2: Kyle only starts cashing out the better toolkit once layered pressure actually stays on the board.
battle-dynamics.phase3: If rewrite never fully opens, the practical edge stays with Manhattan from start to finish.
battle-dynamics.analysis: Kyle owns the fuller profile. Manhattan owns the cleaner first move.

x-factor.headline: X-FACTOR
x-factor.subtitle: The variable that affects the verdict more than ordinary stats.
x-factor.mechanika: Kyle only needs one real Life Equation window, but Manhattan's whole game is stopping that window before it exists.
x-factor.implikacja: If Kyle gets the full setup, the matchup flips. If Manhattan acts first, the better toolkit stays theoretical.
x-factor.psychologia: Kyle wants options to multiply. Manhattan wants the fight to stay singular and unfinished.

interpretation.headline: INTERPRETATION
interpretation.subtitle: Who wins the fight on paper?
interpretation.line1: Kyle owns the broader profile, better fighting rhythm, and the more complete active toolkit.
interpretation.line2: Manhattan still leads the default fight because he can attack the setup itself before Kyle's best route fully exists.
interpretation.line3: Paper advantage does not survive if the fight never reaches symmetrical exchange terms.
interpretation.quote: Kyle wins the categories. Manhattan wins the part where the fight becomes real.

fight-simulation.headline: FIGHT SIMULATION
fight-simulation.subtitle: The course of the fight across three phases.
fight-simulation.opening: Kyle tries to seize initiative through speed, constructs, and layered White Light pressure.
fight-simulation.midFight: Manhattan refuses normal exchange logic and attacks the setup, ring timing, or local state of the move.
fight-simulation.lateFight: The fight diverges on one question only: whether Kyle gets a real Life Equation window before preemption lands.
fight-simulation.endCondition: This fight is decided by whether symmetry ever forms at all.

stat-trap.headline: STAT TRAP
stat-trap.subtitle: Why better stats do not guarantee victory
stat-trap.trapTop: BETTER STATS DO NOT MATTER IF THE SETUP NEVER FULLY FORMS
stat-trap.trapBottom: MANHATTAN WINS BY DENYING THE BOARD, NOT BY WINNING A NORMAL DUEL
stat-trap.example: Kyle can be better on paper and still lose the default fight if Manhattan erases the action before rewrite comes online.
stat-trap.question: Can Kyle force a real rewrite window before Manhattan attacks the setup itself?

verdict-matrix.headline: VERDICT MATRIX
verdict-matrix.subtitle: Victory depends on the rules.
verdict-matrix.case1: Dr. Manhattan 6.5/10. Full rewrite keeps Kyle live, but proactive preemption still steals enough openings to stay slightly ahead.
verdict-matrix.case2: Dr. Manhattan 9/10. Limited rewrite plus proactive preemption removes the only branch that really changes the matchup.
verdict-matrix.case3: Kyle 7/10. If Manhattan becomes passive and Kyle reaches full expression, the broader toolkit finally cashes out.
verdict-matrix.case4: Dr. Manhattan 6.5/10. Passivity narrows the gap, but limited Life Equation access still leaves Kyle too dependent on a setup Manhattan can unravel.
